subject: FinVista trial traffic characteristics & next-step checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@finvista.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@finvista.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinVista trial traffic characteristics & next-step checklist

Hi Helen / Rajiv — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have a single place to iterate on details before we spin up the trial environment. Please correct me where I missed something.

Goal (trial success criteria)
- Validate 14-day evaluation window with representative traffic (production-shaped).
- Meet 95th-percentile latency < 400ms for the primary prompt path at baseline throughput.
- Verify cost-per-1k tokens within expected band for the dedicated instance profile.
- No functional regressions vs your current inference output on the 10 canonical test prompts you shared.

Traffic profile (as discussed) — initial baseline we want to emulate:
- Average RPS: 40 sustained (customer expects bursty patterns).
- Peak RPS (burst): 220 for short spikes (10–30s).
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens in, ~220 tokens generated (average sequence length = 340 tokens total).
- 95th percentile token length: ~700 tokens.
- Concurrency target: 55 concurrent requests at baseline, up to 300 during peak bursts.
- Dominant workload: chat-like completions with occasional long summarization jobs (~1% of traffic).

Observability / success measurement
- We'll collect per-token latency and cost buckets, and run the 10 canonical prompts nightly to detect quality regressions.
- SRE telemetry: request/response sizes, KV-cache hit rate, tail latency snapshots, and error rates.

Open questions / assumptions
1) Do you have an exact sampling of token-length distribution (buckets) you can share?
2) Are there ACL or IP-restriction constraints for our test harness to reach your prod-like endpoints?
3) Any compliance attachments we should know about (data retention, masking rules)?

Next steps and owners (proposed)
- Helen/Rajiv: share sample payloads and a short token-length histogram (owner: FinVista) — due Wed 6/17.
- Redwood (Marissa): propose a dedicated baseline config (GPU profile, memory, batch tuning) by Thu 6/18.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare the canary rollout plan and rollback criteria; sync w/ FinVista SRE — due Mon 6/22.
- Karthik: schedule trial start (tentative 6/24) and own end-to-end readiness check.

Attachments: placeholder for any sample payloads or runbook items you send — we’ll ingest them into the trial harness.

Thanks — I’ll update this thread when we receive the sample payloads and when Marissa posts the baseline config.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — that aligns well with what we went over. Couple clarifications and we attached the sample payloads you requested.

Clarifications:
- The "peak burst" number of ~220 RPS is observed during business-hour throttles from our mobile traffic; bursts last 10–45s, usually ~20s.
- The long-summary requests are heavy (avg 1.2k tokens generated) but are <1% of overall traffic.
- Token-length histogram attached (see finvista_sample_payloads.json) — it includes 48h of anonymized request sizes and a small set of canonical prompts.

Operational notes:
- Our SRE team (sre@finvista.com) will want a network allowlist for the test harness IPs; copying them on this thread.
- We have a documented retention policy: user-level input is purged after 30 days; we'll provide a short note for your compliance team.

Attachments: finvista_sample_payloads.json (anonymized request list), token_histogram.csv

Appreciate you capturing the owners. Looking forward to Marissa's config recommendation.

Best,
Helen Park
Head of Product Operations, FinVista
helen.park@finvista.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinVista trial traffic characteristics & next-step checklist

Karthik / Ben — quickly read the sample payloads Helen sent. A couple of operational checks before I post the baseline config this afternoon: 

1) For the baseline we want to size for sustained 40 RPS and a concurrency headroom of 3x (so target ~120 concurrent). If FinVista expects 55 concurrency baseline per Karthik’s note, can you confirm which number we should pick for initial capacity?
2) The long-summary heavy jobs (1.2k generated tokens) will change batching behavior and memory footprint — recommend we isolate that path on a separate route to avoid oversized batches affecting tail latency. Thoughts?
3) Ben — can you confirm we can offer a short SLA window for the 6/24 start (48–72 hours of accelerated monitoring) and that the canary plan includes automatic fallback to the hosted model variant if tail latency exceeds 700ms?

I’ll attach a draft of the GPU profile and expected performance bands when I reply later.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — quick updated plan after the inputs from Helen and Marissa. Summary for scheduling and owners: 

1) Trial start date: 2026-06-24 (two-week evaluation window).
2) Baseline capacity: provision for 55 concurrency baseline, tuned to handle sustained 40 RPS; we’ll provision burst headroom to absorb 220 RPS spikes with autoscaling parameters. (Owner: Marissa)
3) Heavy long-summary route: isolated route with limited concurrency and separate batch sizing; route will be throttled at 5% of global tokens to protect latency. (Owner: Marissa + FinVista SRE)
4) Observability and regression checks: nightly run of the 10 canonical prompts, token-level cost metrics, 95/99 latency snapshots and KV cache hit-rate. (Owner: Karthik)
5) Network allowlist: FinVista SRE to provide the IP ranges by EOD Thu 6/18. Once we have that, Redwood ops will add them to the trial harness. (Owner: FinVista SRE)
6) Canary / fallback: Ben to publish rollback criteria in HubSpot and post the canary runbook link here. Automatic fallback to hosted model variant if 95th latency > 700ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows. (Owner: Ben)
7) Compliance note: FinVista to provide the short retention policy doc; Redwood compliance will confirm acceptable handling. (Owner: Helen)

Attachments included in thread: finvista_sample_payloads.json, sre_runbook_v1.pdf, poctraffic_sla_table.csv
Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/finvista/poc-plan, https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456789

I’ll block an ops readiness call for Wed 6/23 to walk through the canary steps and network setup. If anyone objects to the timeline or owners, flag now and we’ll update.

—Karthik
